Where to Stay in Trat?
12 Hotels We Actually Reviewed

heroSub: 12 hand-picked Trat hotels across every budget — from 5-star beachfront pool villas on Koh Chang and Koh Kood down to a Klong Prao dorm from ฿550/night. Covering the main areas: Koh Chang, Koh Kood, Koh Mak and Trat Town. From roughly ฿550–9,000/night.
heroStats: 🏝️ 4 key areas (Koh Chang·Koh Kood·Koh Mak·Trat Town)
introH2: 🏝️ Why does choosing the right island and area in Trat matter so much?
introHtml: Trat isn't a single island — each one has a completely different vibe. Koh Chang is the biggest, with several beaches, restaurants, nightlife and the easiest access: it's only a 30–45 min ferry from the Trat-side piers (White Sand Beach, Klong Prao, Kai Bae). Koh Kood is further out and much quieter — clear water, beautiful beaches, ideal if you genuinely want to escape, but it's a 1–1.5 hour speedboat ride. Koh Mak is a small island in between, calm and flat enough to cycle around. And Trat Town isn't on the sea but is cheap and handy for a night before an early boat. Many people book without checking how far an island is, then lose a whole day shuttling back and forth by boat. This guide rounds up 12 Trat hotels we've already reviewed across every tier — with real guest-review scores, a 3-site price comparison and direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Trat has no metro, and the key thing is that almost every stay in this guide is on an island, so you'll take a boat. The main piers for Koh Chang are Center Point and Ao Thammachat — a 30–45 min ferry, then a songthaew on the island. For Koh Kood and Koh Mak you take a speedboat from Laem Sok or a private pier: roughly 45–60 min to Koh Mak and 1–1.5 hours to Koh Kood. From Trat Airport (TDX) it's about 30–40 min to the Koh Chang piers. The areas in this guide: Koh Chang — the big island, several beaches, easiest access (White Sand·Klong Prao·Kai Bae) · Koh Kood — far, quiet, clear water, beautiful beaches · Koh Mak — small, calm, cycle around the island · Trat Town — cheap, handy before an early boat.

entries.name: Dinso Resort & Villas Ko Chang

rooms.type: King Premium Sea View Pool Access

entries.addr: Klong Prao Beach, Ko Chang, Trat
entries.storyHtml: The top score in this guide at 9.4 — Dinso is a 5-star beachfront resort on Klong Prao under IHG's Vignette Collection, starting from just ฿4,500. The draw is modern design and big-chain service standards at a price well below the usual luxury resorts on Koh Chang. Real guest reviews praise the fresh, stylish rooms, the beachfront location and breakfast, though some note Klong Prao gets shallow and rocky at low tide. A great fit if you want 5-star on Koh Chang without paying pool-villa rates.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: the entry-level Deluxe Premium is already fresh and stylish — only step up to Sea View Pool Access if you want to walk straight into the pool from your terrace. Take the ferry from the Trat-side pier and arrange a transfer or songthaew on the island.
pros: Top score in the guide, 9.4 — consistent across Booking and Agoda
Vignette Collection by IHG — big-chain service standards
Modern design, fresh rooms, right on Klong Prao Beach
From ฿4,500 — 5-star luxury at a reachable price
cons: Klong Prao gets shallow and rocky at low tide
On Koh Chang — you take a ferry and a ride on the island

entries.name: Santhiya Tree Koh Chang Resort
entries.addr: 8/8 Moo 4, Klong Prao Beach, Ko Chang, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Santhiya Tree is a luxury resort from the Santhiya group, built around teakwood villas in lush tropical gardens on Klong Prao Beach, scoring 9.4. The standout is the carved teakwood and the calm, private garden setting, with rooms ranging from garden villas up to Pool Access and Hideaway Pool Villas. Real guest reviews love the atmosphere and craftsmanship, but note some villas sit on a slope with steps, and rates start noticeably higher than Dinso. Ideal for couples and honeymooners who love woodwork and gardens.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: the entry Deluxe Villa is already beautiful — step up to Villa Pool Access only if you want a private pool. Ask about villa location when booking; if you'd rather avoid the slope, request a unit near the central areas.
pros: Teakwood villas in lush gardens — private luxury-resort feel
Scores 9.4 — reviews praise the décor and the calm
Several room types, from garden villas to Pool Access
On Klong Prao Beach — great for couples and honeymoons
cons: Entry rates run noticeably higher than Dinso
Some villas are on a slope with steps

entries.name: Shantaa Resort, Kohkood
tags: 🌿 Garden villas on a hillside, sea views
🛁 Open-air bathrooms with a garden tub
entries.addr: Ao Tapao, Moo 2, Ko Kut, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Shantaa is a 4-star boutique resort scoring a high 9.4 from around 385 reviews — the highest score and most reviews in the 4-star tier here. The draw is 24 villas spread through lush hillside gardens at Ao Tapao on Koh Kood, with strong privacy and the open-air bathrooms with a garden bathtub that nearly every review mentions. There's an infinity pool with sea views, a quiet private beach, and a breakfast that gets repeated praise. Real guest reviews love the atmosphere and service, but note some villas are small, rooms have no TV (by design), and Koh Kood is far. Ideal for couples and anyone after a quiet retreat.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: if your budget allows, step up to an Extra Sweet for much more space — some face the sunset. Rooms have no TV by design, so screen-lovers should know in advance. Check ferry times from Trat and book ahead, as there are only 24 villas.
pros: Scores 9.4 · well-reviewed (385) — top of the 4-star tier
Hillside garden villas with strong privacy and sea views
Open-air bathrooms with a garden tub · infinity pool · quiet private beach
Repeatedly praised breakfast — great for couples and honeymoons
cons: Some villas are small, and rooms have no TV (by design)
Koh Kood is far — a 1–1.5 hour ferry ride

entries.name: High Season Pool Villa & Spa Koh Kood
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Klong Chao Beach · Koh Kood · every room has a private pool
tags: 🏊 Every room is a private-pool villa
entries.addr: 117 Moo 2, Klong Chao Beach, Ko Kut, Trat
entries.storyHtml: High Season is a pool-villa resort on Koh Kood where every room has its own private pool, and it's the most-reviewed luxury stay here — over 804 reviews at 9.2. The draw is a private pool villa on quiet Koh Kood, with clear water and beautiful beaches — a genuine escape. Real guest reviews praise the privacy and in-room pools, but are clear that Koh Kood is far (a 1–1.5 hour speedboat) and dining outside the resort is limited. Best for a longer, stay-put holiday.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Koh Kood is far — plan a multi-night stay to make the trip worthwhile. Check speedboat times and book ahead; during monsoon (May–Oct) some crossings are cancelled. The entry Deluxe Pool Villa already comes with a private pool.
pros: Every room is a private-pool villa — very private
Most-reviewed luxury stay, 804 · consistent 9.2
On quiet Koh Kood with clear water and lovely beaches
On-site spa — perfect for a longer holiday
cons: Koh Kood is far — a 1–1.5 hour speedboat ride
Limited dining outside the resort; not easy to get around

entries.name: Awa Koh Chang
tags: 🏖️ Kai Bae — quieter than White Sand
entries.addr: 12/3 Moo 4, Kai Bae Beach, Ko Chang, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Awa is a modern-design 4-star boutique beach resort on Kai Bae Beach with a healthy 460 reviews at 8.9. The draw is the contemporary design and a Kai Bae location that's quieter than White Sand Beach but still has restaurants and bars nearby. The entry Superior Hillside sits in the garden across the road and starts at just ฿1,800. Real guest reviews praise the design and value, but note the entry rooms aren't beachfront — you cross the road to the sea side.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: if you want to be on the sea side and walk down to the beach, step up to a Deluxe in the main resort grounds near the pool/sea. Kai Bae has lovely sunsets in the evening.
pros: Modern design, well-reviewed (460) · 8.9
Kai Bae is quieter than White Sand but still has eateries nearby
From just ฿1,800 for a 4-star
Range of rooms, from Hillside to a Beachfront Suite

On Koh Chang — you take a ferry and a ride on the island

entries.name: KC Grande Resort & Spa
entries.mrtTag: 📍 White Sand Beach · Koh Chang · beach side + hill side
tags: 🏖️ On White Sand Beach, walk onto the sand
entries.addr: 1/1 Moo 4, White Sand Beach (Hat Sai Khao), Ko Chang, Trat
entries.storyHtml: KC Grande is a 4-star resort right on White Sand Beach with a strong 497 reviews at 8.9. The draw is a central spot on Koh Chang's most popular beach — you can walk onto the sand, with restaurants and bars all around. There's a beach side and a (newer) hill side, plus Family Suites. Real guest reviews praise the location and service, but note White Sand Beach is lively and gets crowded in high season. Best if you want to be in the middle of the action on Koh Chang.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: for newer, quieter rooms choose the hill side; to walk straight onto the sand pick a beach-side Deluxe. Request a room away from the road/bars if you want a quiet night.
pros: Right on White Sand Beach — walk onto the sand
Well-reviewed (497) · consistent 8.9
Both beach side and hill side, several room tiers
Family Suites and a spa — good for families
cons: White Sand Beach is lively and gets crowded in high season
Some beach-side rooms are near bars; can be noisy at night

entries.name: Seavana Beach Resort Koh Mak
entries.badge: 🌅 Sea-view rooms on the beach, Koh Mak
entries.addr: 1/23 Moo 2, Ao Suan Yai, Ko Mak, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Seavana is a beachfront resort on Koh Mak where every room is a sea view, scoring a high 9.3. The draw is the Ao Suan Yai location with full sunset views, and Koh Mak's calm vibe — flat enough to cycle around. Real guest reviews praise the views and the quiet, but honestly the review count is still low (25) compared with others here. Great for couples and anyone after a small, quiet island at 3-star prices.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Koh Mak is small and quiet with no nightlife — renting a bicycle or scooter to ride around the island is the most fun. The Deluxe Beachfront is closest to the water if you want to wake up to the sea.
pros: Every room is sea view, with full sunset views
High score, 9.3 · on Ao Suan Yai beach
Calm Koh Mak — perfect for cycling around the island

entries.name: Mira Montra Resort Koh Mak
entries.addr: Ao Phra Beach, Moo 1, Ko Mak, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Mira Montra is a 4-star boutique resort on Ao Phra Beach, Koh Mak, built around sea-view rooms and private villas, scoring 9.0. The draw is a mix of hilltop sea-view rooms and beachfront villas, plus a 2-bedroom Family Villa for families or groups of friends. Real guest reviews praise the views and Koh Mak's calm, though the review count is still modest (66) and some villas sit on a slope with steps. A good fit for a villa on a small island at mid-range prices.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: groups and families should look at the 2-bedroom Family Villa, which works out cheaper per head. For waking up to the sea, choose a Beachfront Deluxe Villa.

entries.name: Chang Buri Resort & Spa
entries.badge: 💰 Great value, beach side + hill side
entries.mrtTag: 📍 South end of White Sand Beach · Koh Chang
tags: 🌿 South end of White Sand, quieter
entries.addr: 99 Moo 4, White Sand Beach (Hat Sai Khao), Ko Chang, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Chang Buri is a well-priced 3-star beach resort at the south end of White Sand Beach, from just ฿1,600, scoring 8.7. It sits at the quieter end of White Sand and has both a sea side and a hill side (with views over the bay), plus Pool Side Villas and a Pool Villa for those who want to upgrade. Real guest reviews praise the value and the bay-view pool, but note the hill-side rooms involve a climb and some parts are dated. Good for mid-budget travellers who want the White Sand zone without the crowds.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: the Superior Hillside is the cheapest and is near the bay-view pool, but you climb the hill to reach it. For something closer to the water, choose a Deluxe Seaside.
pros: From ฿1,600 — great value for the White Sand zone
Both sea side and hill side, with bay views
Pool Side Villa and Pool Villa for upgraders
South end of White Sand — quieter than the centre
cons: Hill-side rooms involve a climb up the slope
Some parts are dated — ask for a renovated room

entries.name: Trat City Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Trat Town · not on the sea
entries.addr: 411/17 Moo 2, Wang Krachae, Mueang Trat, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Trat City Hotel is the cheapest stay in this guide, from just ฿900, yet it scores a high 9.2. The draw is a central Trat Town location — handy for a night before an early island boat, or for the night you come back from the islands before flying out. Rooms are clean with a private balcony, TV and fridge. Real guest reviews praise the cleanliness and value, but it's clearly a town hotel, not on the sea. Best for budget travellers and anyone using Trat Town as a transit base.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: use it for your first or last night before/after the islands to save time and money. Check morning boat times with the pier in advance, as some depart very early.
pros: Cheapest in the guide, ฿900 · high score 9.2
Central Trat Town — handy before/after island boats
Clean rooms with a balcony, TV and fridge
Great value for budget travellers and transit stays
cons: Not on the sea — it's a town hotel
You still travel on to a pier to reach the islands

entries.name: Koh Kood Resort
entries.addr: 45 Moo 5, Bang Bao Bay, Ko Kut, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Koh Kood Resort is a beachfront bungalow resort on Bang Bao Bay that gets you onto Koh Kood at a 3-star budget, from ฿2,500, scoring 8.2. The draw is simple garden bungalows by the beach with a back-to-nature feel, from garden views up to a Sea View Bungalow. Real guest reviews praise the beachfront spot and the quiet, but note the rooms and facilities are simple in the island style, and Koh Kood is far — which is why it lands near the end. Good for mid-budget travellers who want Koh Kood without paying pool-villa rates.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: for waking up to the sea, choose a Sea View Bungalow. Koh Kood is far — plan a multi-night stay and check speedboat times ahead; some crossings are cancelled in monsoon.
pros: Gets you onto Koh Kood on a 3-star budget, from ฿2,500
Garden bungalows by the beach, back-to-nature feel
Sea View Bungalow for those who want a sea view
Bang Bao Bay is quiet and relaxing

entries.name: Pajamas Koh Chang
entries.addr: 18/22 Moo 4, Klong Prao Beach, Ko Chang, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Pajamas is the cheapest stay in this guide — dorms from just ฿550 — and well-reviewed with 830 reviews at 8.8. The draw is the stylish design, a swimming pool and a social vibe where it's easy to meet other travellers. Dorms have bunk beds with privacy curtains and personal reading lights, there's a female-only dorm, and a Deluxe Double for those who want a private room. Real guest reviews praise the design, the pool and the value, but it's clearly a hostel — not for those who want a lot of privacy.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: backpackers after the best value should book a dorm; if you want privacy but still want to stay here, choose the pool-view Deluxe Double. It's on Klong Prao — rent a scooter to reach the other beaches easily.
pros: Cheapest in the guide, ฿550 · well-reviewed, 830
Stylish design hostel with a swimming pool
Dorm beds with curtains and reading lights · female-only dorm

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Trat hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which island should I stay on in Trat?
faq.a: It depends on your style. Koh Chang is the big island — several beaches, restaurants, nightlife and the easiest access (Dinso, Santhiya Tree, Awa, KC Grande, Chang Buri, Pajamas). Koh Kood is further and quieter, with clear water and lovely beaches, ideal to escape (Shantaa, High Season, Koh Kood Resort). Koh Mak is a small, calm island you can cycle around (Seavana, Mira Montra). And Trat Town is cheap and handy before a boat (Trat City Hotel).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Trat hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: dorms and hostels start around ฿550–600 a night; town hotels and mid-range to 4-star resorts run roughly ฿900–4,500; pool villas and 5-star beachfront resorts start around ฿8,000–9,000+. All prices are approximate starting rates for standard rooms, and during High Season (Nov–Apr) they run well above normal.

faq.q: ❓ How do I get to Koh Chang, Koh Kood and Koh Mak?
faq.a: Almost every stay in Trat is on an island, so you take a boat. Koh Chang is a 30–45 min ferry from Center Point or Ao Thammachat pier, then a songthaew on the island. Koh Mak is about a 45–60 min speedboat, and Koh Kood about 1–1.5 hours. From Trat Airport (TDX) it's roughly 30–40 min to the Koh Chang piers. In monsoon, speedboats to Koh Kood and Koh Mak may be cancelled on some days — check the weather first.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Trat hotel?
faq.a: For weekdays outside the tourist season, 2–4 weeks ahead is enough. But during High Season (November–April), especially New Year and Songkran, pool villas and beachfront resorts on the islands sell out fast — book 1–2 months ahead. During monsoon (May–Oct) prices drop, but some resorts on Koh Kood and Koh Mak close seasonally, so check before booking.

faq.q: ❓ When is the best time to visit Trat, and is it open year-round?
faq.a: The best window is November–April: calm seas, clear water and good weather. During monsoon (May–October) the sea is rough, it rains, speedboats to Koh Kood and Koh Mak may be cancelled on some days, and some resorts on the smaller islands close seasonally. Koh Chang is the big island, open almost year-round and easier to reach — if you go during monsoon, Koh Chang is safer and more convenient than Koh Kood or Koh Mak.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Trat hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) vary by promotion and season, so it's worth comparing all three before you book — each review page in this guide has price-comparison links. That can save you several hundred to over a thousand baht a night during peak periods.
